title: Yellow Buttery Japanese Squash Jjigae
description: A peppery and flaky Hokkaido Japanese dish made with butternut squash, a rich mother sauce base, and Mediterranean-friendly ingredients, served in a traditional inarizushi form.
instructions: Combine the sushi rice and water in a medium saucepan and bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to low and cover, cooking for 15 minutes or until the water is absorbed and the rice is fluffy.
In a separate pan, melt the butter over medium heat and add the ground ginger and minced garlic, cooking for 1 minute or until fragrant.
Add the miso paste and soy sauce to the pan, whisking until smooth, then add the sesame oil and whisk until combined.
Add the cooked butternut squash to the pan, stirring to coat with the sauce, then season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Cut the inari tofu into quarters and place them on a plate, then spoon the butternut squash mixture on top of the tofu.
Sprinkle the chopped green onions and sesame seeds over the top of the squash mixture, then serve in the inari tofu cups.
Cook the sushi rice according to the package instructions, then let cool to room temperature.
Cut the butternut squash into 1-inch cubes and steam until tender, then let cool to room temperature.
Cut the inari tofu into quarters and cook in a pan with a little bit of oil until crispy on the outside and tender on the inside, then let cool to room temperature.
Cut the cooked butternut squash into small pieces and mix with the cooked sushi rice, then season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Spoon the butternut squash and rice mixture into the inari tofu cups, then top with the green onions and sesame seeds.
Serve the squash and rice mixture in the inari tofu cups hot, garnished with additional green onions and sesame seeds if desired, and a side of soy sauce for serving if desired.
